stories.headline: Super Micro plans $7B equity raise to fund $39B in AI server component purchases

key_facts.fact: Super Micro announced a $7.0 billion series of concurrent equity and equity-linked financing transactions on June 9, 2026 to fund AI server component purchases.
key_facts.excerpt: Super Micro Computer, Inc. (NASDAQ: SMCI), a Total IT Solution Manufacturer for AI, Cloud, Storage, and 5G/Edge, today announced a series of concurrent equity and equity-linked financing transactions totaling $7.0 billion.

key_facts.fact: The package consists of a $1.25B common stock offering, a $3.75B depositary share offering, and a $2B at-the-market program starting no earlier than Q3 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Concurrent underwritten offerings: $5.0 billion underwritten public offerings, consisting of: (1) approximately $1.25 billion of common stock and (2) approximately $3.75 billion of depositary shares; and At-the-market offering: up to $2.0 billion.

key_facts.fact: Proceeds will fund components for approximately $39 billion of recent AI server orders from more than 20 customers.
key_facts.excerpt: Use of net proceeds to fund the purchase of components to satisfy the approximately $39 billion of orders that the Company has received in recent weeks for its advanced AI servers, including its Data Center Building Block Solutions, from more than 20 customers.

key_facts.fact: SMCI shares fell 8% in extended trading on dilution concerns despite the order backlog.
key_facts.excerpt: Super Micro Computer Inc(NASDAQ: SMCI) shares are tumbling in extended trading Tuesday after the company announced a proposed offering to fund AI orders. While the order backlog signals strong demand, investors are reacting to the dilution risk from $7 billion in new equity hitting the market.

stories.headline: AMD-only cloud TensorWave raises $350M Series B at $1.55B valuation led by AMD and Magnetar

key_facts.fact: Las Vegas-based TensorWave raised $350M in a Series B round led by AMD and hedge fund Magnetar Capital, valuing the company at $1.55B.
key_facts.excerpt: Cloud-computing startup TensorWave Inc., which exclusively uses Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) technology instead of Nvidia products, was valued at $1.55 billion after raising $350 million in a Series B funding round led by AMD and hedge fund Magnetar Capital, The Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

key_facts.fact: The new round nearly quadrupled TensorWave's valuation from roughly $400 million a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: The new investment nearly quadrupled TensorWave's valuation from roughly $400 million a year ago. The company was founded in 2023 and positions itself as an alternative to Nvidia, whose chips dominate the artificial intelligence infrastructure market.

key_facts.fact: TensorWave operates an 8,192 AMD Instinct MI325X GPU 'dedicated training' cluster and plans to use the capital to expand data center capacity and buy more chips from AMD.
key_facts.excerpt: TensorWave recently deployed a 'dedicated training' cluster of around 8,000 AMD Instinct MI325X GPUs. The new capital will enable the company to grow that cluster, as well as expand headcount and support 'operational growth,' said Horton.

key_facts.fact: CEO Darrick Horton said the company was created to 'restore competition to the market' against Nvidia's dominance.
key_facts.excerpt: TensorWave's Chief Executive Darrick Horton said the company was created to 'restore competition to the market,' adding, 'I don't like buying things from monopolies. You don't have a lot of leverage.'

stories.headline: OpenAI in talks to lease 10GW Ohio data center on federal land with Nvidia financial backing

key_facts.fact: OpenAI is in advanced negotiations to lease a proposed 10 GW data center campus on federal land in Ohio, with potential financial backing from Nvidia.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI is in negotiations to lease a proposed 10-gigawatt data center campus on federal land in Ohio, in a deal that could include financial backing from Nvidia, The Information reported on Tuesday, citing two people with direct knowledge of the discussions.

key_facts.fact: The campus could cost at least $500 billion if fully built out, based on current prices for chips, labor, power and other materials.
key_facts.excerpt: The campus would be among the largest of its kind. The total cost of the facility could reach at least $500 billion if fully built out, based on current prices for chips, labor, power and other materials.

key_facts.fact: The site is the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Pike County, Ohio, where SoftBank's SB Energy is building 10 GW of new power generation under a March DOE partnership.
key_facts.excerpt: The data center would sit on federal land at the former Portsmouth Gaseous Diffusion Plant in Pike County, Ohio. In March 2026, the US Department of Energy announced a partnership with SoftBank Group and its subsidiary SB Energy to redevelop the site, with SB Energy committing to build 10 GW of new power generation capacity, including at least 9.2 GW from natural gas.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI would control the equipment under a long-term lease, with first-phase operations targeted to begin in 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI would control the equipment in the facility under a long-term lease. The company would be responsible for payments once the project starts operations. The first phase is expected to begin in 2028, the report said.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia and OpenAI signed a letter of intent in September 2025 for at least 10 GW of Nvidia systems, with Nvidia committing up to $100 billion as capacity comes online.
key_facts.excerpt: In September 2025, Nvidia and OpenAI signed a letter of intent for at least 10 gigawatts of Nvidia systems, with Nvidia committing up to $100 billion in OpenAI as capacity comes online. The first gigawatt was targeted for the second half of 2026 using Nvidia's Vera Rubin platform.

stories.headline: Meta partners with Reliance on first India AI data center: 168 MW in Jamnagar, Gujarat

key_facts.fact: Meta and Reliance Industries announced an agreement on June 10 for Meta's first AI-enabled data center in India, with Reliance building a 168 MW facility in Jamnagar, Gujarat that Meta will lease.
key_facts.excerpt: Meta has entered an agreement with Reliance Industries to lease our first AI-enabled data center in India to serve one of our fastest-growing communities. As part of the agreement, Reliance will build a data center with 168 MW capacity, which Meta will lease, with options to scale.

key_facts.fact: The facility will be powered by renewable energy and cooled with desalinated seawater; Meta will cover the full cost of the energy and water supporting the facility.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility will be supported by renewable energy and cooled with desalinated seawater. Meta will cover the full cost of energy and water supporting the facility.

key_facts.fact: Reliance said the 168 MW facility will be ready within two years and can be expanded over time, also supporting Meta's global infrastructure and AI computing requirements.
key_facts.excerpt: Reliance said the 168-megawatt facility will ready within two years and can be expanded over time. Further, the data center will also support Meta's global infrastructure and AI computing requirements, plugging India more directly into the company's worldwide network of AI facilities.

key_facts.fact: Separately, Meta contracted nearly 1 GW of renewable energy capacity in India through agreements with CleanMax and Fourth Partner Energy.
key_facts.excerpt: Separately, Meta said it had contracted nearly 1 gigawatt of new renewable energy capacity in India through agreements with CleanMax and Fourth Partner Energy, which will supplement the renewable power supporting the Jamnagar facility.

key_facts.fact: The deal builds on Meta's $5.7B 2020 investment in Reliance's Jio Platforms and a $100M joint venture last year on enterprise AI solutions.
key_facts.excerpt: The Meta-Reliance agreement marks the latest chapter in a relationship that has steadily deepened since Meta invested $5.7 billion in Jio Platforms in 2020. Since then, the companies have expanded their collaboration across digital services, enterprise AI, and now the infrastructure underpinning next-generation AI systems.

stories.headline: Seattle City Council votes 9-0 for one-year moratorium on new large data centers

key_facts.fact: The Seattle City Council voted unanimously on June 9 to impose a one-year emergency moratorium on new large data centers inside city limits.
key_facts.excerpt: The Seattle City Council voted unanimously Tuesday to impose a one-year emergency moratorium on new large data centers inside the city limits, responding to concerns about the implications of AI for the city's power grid, water supply, utility rates, and economy.

key_facts.fact: The ordinance halts applications for data centers with electrical capacity above 20 megavolt-amperes (roughly 20 MW), enough power for thousands of homes.
key_facts.excerpt: The council approved two measures: an ordinance halting applications for data centers with electrical capacity of more than 20 megavolt-amperes — enough power for thousands of homes — and a resolution committing the city to study their impacts as a precursor to permanent regulations.

key_facts.fact: Mayor Katie Wilson is expected to sign the legislation; the moratorium can be extended for an additional six months and a public hearing must be held within 60 days.
key_facts.excerpt: Under the legislation, data centers are defined as facilities used primarily to store and process digital data, with power capacity exceeding 20 megavolt-amperes and requiring uninterrupted power service. The moratorium could be extended for an additional six months if necessary.

key_facts.fact: Proposed data center projects in Seattle reportedly had combined peak demand equal to about a third of the city's average daily power consumption.
key_facts.excerpt: The moratorium would take effect as soon as Mayor Katie Wilson signs it, temporarily halting projects like several large data centers that companies have approached Seattle City Light about building in the city. Those projects reportedly had a combined peak demand equal to about a third of Seattle's average daily power consumption.

key_facts.fact: The ordinance exempts roughly 30 smaller data centers already operating in Seattle, allowing each to expand by up to another 20 megavolt-amperes.
key_facts.excerpt: The ordinance exempts the roughly 30 smaller data centers already operating in Seattle, allowing each to expand by up to another 20 megavolt-amperes, which is the same amount as the threshold of the moratorium on new facilities.

stories.headline: SK Hynix targets US ADR listing as soon as August, potentially raising up to $14B

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix plans to list its shares in the US as soon as August, seeking to capitalize on AI-stock appetite and broaden its investor base, sources told Reuters.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix plans to list its shares in the US as soon as August, said two sources familiar with the matter, as the South Korean memory chipmaker seeks to capitalise on strong appetite for artificial intelligence (AI)-linked stocks and broaden its investor base.

key_facts.fact: The SEC is expected to approve SK Hynix's American depositary receipt (ADR) listing application during the week of June 22.
key_facts.excerpt: The US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is likely to approve SK Hynix's American depositary receipt (ADR) listing application during the week of June 22, one of the sources said.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix filed confidentially in March, with the offering potentially raising as much as $14B.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix said in March it had confidentially filed for a US listing. A source said at the time that the offering could raise as much as US$14 billion.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix is the world's second-largest memory chipmaker and a key Nvidia supplier of high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips used in AI servers.
key_facts.excerpt: The company, the world's second-largest memory chipmaker and a key supplier to Nvidia, has been one of the biggest beneficiaries of the AI boom due to its dominant position in high-bandwidth memory chips used in AI servers.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix stock has jumped 240% year-to-date and its market cap has surpassed $1 trillion.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix's stock has jumped 240% this year and its market cap has surpassed $1 trillion.

stories.headline: Standard Bots raises $200M Series C at $1B valuation to scale US-made AI robot arms

key_facts.fact: Standard Bots announced on June 9 a $200M Series C led by RoboStrategy and existing investor General Catalyst at a $1 billion valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: NEW YORK, June 9, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Standard Bots, America's largest manufacturer of AI-native, industrial robotics, today announced a $200 million Series C led by RoboStrategy and existing investors including General Catalyst at a $1 billion valuation.

key_facts.fact: The round is a significant step up from the $63M Standard Bots raised in 2024 at an undisclosed valuation.
key_facts.excerpt: Standard Bots has closed a $200mn round that values the company at $1bn, minting a fresh robotics unicorn. The financing was led by General Catalyst and RoboStrategy, a fund dedicated to robotics, and marks a steep step up from the $63mn the company raised in 2024 at an undisclosed valuation.

key_facts.fact: The company makes AI-native robot arms and industrial humanoids deployed at customers including Sunoco, Amazon, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the US Army.
key_facts.excerpt: Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots, trusted by hundreds of customers, from large enterprises like Sunoco, Amazon, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army to hundreds of SMB manufacturers across nearly every state.

key_facts.fact: The capital will fund expansion of the Glen Cove, New York manufacturing facility; the company plans by 2027 to manufacture everything 'from metal in to robots out' in the US.
key_facts.excerpt: Standard Bots designs almost all its own parts, including its own actuators, assembles every final product in-house, and by 2027, plans to manufacture everything – from metal in to robots out – right here in America.

key_facts.fact: Standard Bots' robots are taught by demonstration rather than code, with AI running in the background to learn tasks.
key_facts.excerpt: The company builds robotic arms, the kind that automate industrial work such as complex assembly and loading and unloading machines. Its pitch is that the arms can learn a new task after simply watching a demonstration of it, thanks to AI running in the background, rather than needing an engineer to hand-code every movement.
